General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

Renting as a financial strategy, what real estate agents should know

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that renting isn’t always a stepping stone to homeownership.
  • The story we’re telling ourselves about renters is outdated, Virginia Love, industry principal at Entrata, told me recently.
  • Industry observers note that entrata is a property management operating system built to improve operational efficiency at multifamily communities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that renting isn’t always a stepping stone to homeownership. Multifamily expert Virginia Love of Entrata explains how financial priorities, flexibility and the true cost of ownership are reshaping renters’ decisions.

The story we’re telling ourselves about renters is outdated, Virginia Love, industry principal at Entrata, told me recently.

Industry observers note that entrata is a property management operating system built to improve operational efficiency at multifamily communities. In its recent “Resident Pulse” survey, conducted in partnership with YouGov, the firm asked renters about their financial priorities, attitudes toward homeownership, definitions of success and other lifestyle factors.

That gives Love a bird’s-eye view of the state of renting and, by extension, homeownership.

It has been revealed that “I feel like people think that renters are less-than,” she remarked. “I think the real story is, people are trying to do what’s right for them and what’s right for their family.”.

Industry observers note that with homeownership increasingly out of reach for people of all ages, it’s time that real estate agents rethink the role of renters in the housing market. Entrata’s insights can help.

Love said that renters are prioritizing healthy financial hygiene and making decisions based on a more complex economic environment, reducing their existing financial obligations before pursuing longer-term financial goals.

“They are eating out less, they’re shopping less, they’re spending less, they’re switching to cheaper brands,” she noted, with the goal of prioritizing emergency savings, debt reduction and other budgetary line items.

According to recent reports, for previous generations, the initial barrier to homeownership was a down payment, Love remarked. Now, it’s the rising costs of everything that comes after the initial upfront purchase price: the mortgage payment at today’s higher rates, insurance, maintenance, repairs and other expenses. Managing the unexpected requires greater levels of financial stability.

“It’s then I have insurance, then I gotta take care of the yard. Then what if the tree falls on the driveway?” Love noted.

According to recent reports, beyond the cost of rent vs. buy, maintenance, amenities and the ability to relocate can have real value for renters, especially when they’re working to pay down debt, pursuing educational goals, navigating career shifts or deciding where and when they’re ready to settle down. What they’re paying for, Love said, is freedom.

Love describes Gen Z in particular as pragmatic about money and more willing to take a gradual path toward major financial milestones.

For those who strategy to buy, “they’re absolutely fine with starter homes,” Love remarked. “And I don’t think that that is something that we’ve seen for a while. Everybody kind of wanted to go from zero to 60, and this is a generation that’s willing to take those steps.”.

She explains that some renters are working toward a purchase while others prefer to invest, maintain flexibility or avoid being tied to one address.

Industry observers note that real estate agents often approach renters with an ingrained belief in the superiority of homeownership, but it’s not right for everyone. Spend time upfront with renters to find out what matters to them, and don’t just push them toward homeownership automatically, Love noted.

Stop assuming buying is the client’s next step: Renters aren’t necessarily buyers who simply haven’t saved up a down payment yet. They may have other financial priorities, like paying down student loans, building an emergency fund, investing for retirement or prioritizing flexibility. Ask what a client’s financial priorities are before assuming homeownership is the goal.

Talk about the full cost of homeownership: Down payments aren’t the whole story here. Monthly payments, rising insurance and repair costs, home maintenance and other expenses can affect whether, and when, buying makes sense. Make sure you’re sharing updated costs of ownership along with the upfront costs, and be realistic about affordability.

Industry observers note that ask what payment feels comfortable, not just what a lender will approve: A client’s maximum purchasing power isn’t necessarily the same as their target budget. Understand the buying budget that matches their comfort level, other financial considerations and personal priorities before locking in on a price range.

Understand that delay isn’t the same as giving up: Some renters may aspire to own a home, but they’re not necessarily in a rush. Maintain relationships over the long haul without turning every conversation into a homebuying pitch.

Recognize that renting has value beyond the monthly payment: The benefits of renting — maintenance support, amenities, flexibility and freedom — may outweigh those of homeownership, even though they don’t build equity for the renter. Understand what the renter values before presenting ownership as an obvious upgrade or superior choice.

Sources indicate that “I think the real story is, people are trying to do what’s right for them and what’s right for their family,” Love remarked. By understanding timing, goals and price sensitivities, agents can help potential clients evaluate their options without prescribing the outcome ahead of time.

Troy Palmquist is the founder of HomeCode Advisors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

Governance platform provider OneTrust LLC today unveiled its Fall ’26 Release, a set of platform updates noted to bring governance into the workflows where business decisions are made.

Building on OneTrust CORIE, a shared intelligence layer for governing artificial intelligence agents introduced at the company’s TrustWeek conference in September, the release covers AI visibility, privacy, consent and third-party risk management.

Leading the list of updates is a revised AI inventory, which is designed to reflect changes across a customer’s environment on a continuous basis. According to OneTrust, the change is needed because many organizations running complex networks of AI systems and agents have only limited visibility into how those systems operate. Model associations, potential matches and deprecation indicators from providers are now pulled into the inventory from a curated library of foundation models.

Relationships among AI systems, models, agents, projects, risks, controls and workflows can be explored through an interactive AI lineage view. AI performance and operational dashboards, added in the release, bring usage, associated risk, evaluation coverage, outbound personally identifiable information discovery and token consumption into one summary.

Ryan Karlin, vice president of product management at OneTrust, stated knowing which AI systems are in the business “is just the starting point.” According to Karlin, teams also need visibility into the activity and dependencies of those systems “alongside the privacy and third-party risks they already manage.”.

On the third-party risk side, a workflow rule that launches a risk assessment can now trigger OneTrust’s Deep Research AI skill. The in-depth research report that the skill compiles from public data sources is then used to answer the assessment questionnaire. OneTrust claims the integration can cut the time needed to complete a third-party risk assessment from weeks to minutes.

Drawing on previous assessments and supplier documentation, the company’s expanded AI Document Scanning and Inventory Response Analysis features can now also answer questions about the business engagement tied to a third party.

According to recent reports, for privacy teams, the release adds protections against automated abuse of data subject request web forms. Growing volumes of those automated requests are straining team workloads, according to OneTrust. To filter out the abuse, enhanced CAPTCHA options now work alongside cross-site request forgery token controls to block suspicious submissions.

In the organization’s consent management platform, navigation, configuration, scanning, publishing and geolocation management have also been brought into a single workflow under a modernized interface.

It has been revealed that rounding out the release are reporting updates. Enhanced assessment reporting and application programming interfaces are stated to give privacy teams more insight into what drives risk scores. New risk hierarchy visualizations, which show how individual risks across business units aggregate into enterprise risk categories, are aimed at helping teams prioritize risk treatment.

OneTrust is sharing availability details for the Fall ’26 Release through an overview webinar.

Industry observers note that oneTrust has raised $1.13 billion to date, including $150 million in 2023 at a valuation of $4.5 billion. Investors in the company include Insight Partners LP, Coatue Management, Technology Crossover Ventures LP, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 LP, Franklin Resources Inc., Generation Investment Management LLP and Sands Capital Management.

OfferUp co-founder sees ‘mini power plants’ in buildings full of EVs

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 12, 2026 at 2:41 pmNovember 12, 2026 at 2:41 pm.

It has been revealed that nick Huzar co-founded Juicer Energy in 2023 to make electric vehicle charging more widespread and reliable. Now the Seattle-area startup is pursuing a broader goal: helping buildings manage rising electricity demand and costs.

Juicer installs and operates EV charging systems at apartment buildings, hotels and other properties. It is also developing battery systems to store electricity on-site and help manage the power needed for charging and other building uses.

The push comes as data centers and the growing use of electricity for transportation, heating and other needs put more pressure on the grid. Batteries can help balance supply and demand by storing energy when electricity is plentiful and releasing it when demand peaks. In some cases, they can reduce the need for costly grid upgrades or newly introduced power plants built to meet peak demand.

In a recent development, “We think there’s a significant opportunity there,” Huzar mentioned. He spoke at an event this week hosted by GeekWire and Bank of America at the Bellevue showroom of Ferrari of Seattle.

Other companies are similarly pairing EV charging with battery storage. Fellow Seattle startup Electric Era has deployed battery-backed fast chargers at retailers including Costco and convenience stores. ADS-TEC Energy and XCharge also sell fast-charging systems with integrated batteries.

Recent findings suggest that huzar, OfferUp’s co-founder and former CEO, sees an opportunity to make buildings more self-sufficient by combining hardware and energy-management software. He stated Juicer has a project scheduled to come online in 2027 with 70 chargers in one building.

His longer-term vision also includes tapping the energy stored in vehicles connected to those buildings.

“Imagine you’re an apartment owner and you have 20 EVs, 40 EVs plugged in,” Huzar remarked. “That is a huge amount of power. Like you’re a mini power plant at that point.”.

Recent findings suggest that he described feeding excess electricity back to the grid as a possibility that remains years away. He also predicted that most businesses, apartments and homes would have on-site batteries within the next decade, in part because battery costs continue to fall.

Juicer started with EV charging, Huzar said, “but the more we’ve gotten into this, the more we realize that we actually can build an asset for buildings versus relying on the grid.”.

Four IPOs Onchain in Under Six Months.

Anthropic offered 825 million Class A shares at an indicated range of $70 to $78 per share, implying a valuation of up to approximately $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

Industry observers note that mantle has listed each major IPO tokenized by xStocks shortly after its public debut. $SPCXx went live on Mantle on June 19, one week after SpaceX's record $85.7 billion IPO on Nasdaq. $BSPx followed on July 7, six days after Bending Spoons listed on Nasdaq. $JMKEx went live in mid-August, following Jersey Mike's debut on the Newly introduced York Stock Exchange on July 30.

These listings are part of Mantle's broader growth in tokenized assets. More than 1,500 tokenized real-world assets are now live on Mantle according to RWA.xyz, up from 71 at the start of 2026. They include Franklin Templeton's US equity index ETF ($USPXx) and $USDG, issued natively on Mantle by Paxos.

Atomic RFQ Execution and Dual Rewards on Fluxion.

Once live on Fluxion, a native DEX on Mantle, $ANTx will trade 24/7 through Atomic RFQ, which executes orders at firm quotes anchored to the underlying security at live market prices, reducing slippage compared to AMM-only execution. People will also be able to provide liquidity to $ANTx pools on Fluxion's AMM and earn trading fees generated by pool volume.

Eligible $ANTx trading and liquidity provision on Fluxion will earn from two exclusive reward programmes concurrently: xPoints, xStocks' native onchain rewards, and Fluxion Points, distributed proportionally by trading volume and liquidity contribution.

Zero-Knowledge Security Built for Institutional Adoption.

Mantle became the first ZK validity rollup with Succinct's SP1 in 2025. Every transaction is proven with zero-knowledge proofs and secured by Ethereum, providing the institutional-grade security required for regulated assets. Anthropic's November 2026 research on provable inference, FlashProve, cites Mantle alongside Starknet as an example of a blockchain network deploying zkSNARKs.

On this foundation, Mantle has onboarded institutional-grade assets including Paxos' $USDG, issued natively under MAS and MiCA oversight, along with Maple's $syrupUSDT, Ethena's $USDe and Ondo's $USDY.

"A company going public used to mean access for some investors in some markets. Tokenization is changing that, and Mantle is built to carry it further," said Emily Bao, Key Advisor at Mantle. "The same infrastructure that institutional issuers trust for their assets now brings the year's most anticipated listings to traders worldwide, around the clock.".

Mantle will continue to list tokenized equities as latest companies go public, connecting each listing to the same onchain infrastructure and distribution channels.

Mantle is the open financial network powering borderless access to global capital markets, connecting global market participants to institutional-grade capital market assets onchain. Mantle brings the full lifecycle of real-world assets onchain, from issuance and liquidity to distribution and settlement, spanning tokenized equities, treasury yield, private credit, commodities, and money markets. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prophetic has launched SiteAI Drafter, a tool that lets land teams draw high-precision, compliant subdivision site plans in minutes and export them directly to CAD.

The company, which describes itself as the operating system for land acquisition, introduced SiteAI Drafter on Tuesday as a new feature designed to help residential land teams move from site concept to engineering faster and at lower upfront cost, according to its announcement.

SiteAI Drafter is now available to all SiteAI users and adds manual, CAD-ready drafting to a platform that has focused primarily on automated layouts and early-stage feasibility analysis.

Sources indicate that siteAI generates subdivision site plans with lot and unit yield that account for setbacks, wetlands, flood zones, open spaces and stormwater ponds. Builders and developers use the system to run feasibility studies in seconds instead of weeks, replacing initial engineering reports that can cost from $3,000 to more than $10,000.

Sources indicate that the platform’s automated layouts estimate maximum theoretical yield and swiftly screen large numbers of parcels. Because SiteAI incorporates site constraints at the outset, it can flag challenges that might not surface until much later in a traditional workflow, when engineering work is further along and sunk costs are higher.

For acquisition and development teams working in a competitive land market, this kind of early, standardized analysis is used to compare sites on a level playing field and decide which deals to advance before ordering surveys or full design work.

Industry observers note that while automated layouts help screen many parcels at once, land teams often have a preferred concept for a specific site based on local jurisdiction standards, topography and planned product types. Under traditional processes, testing that concept typically requires drafting in CAD or waiting for an engineer, which can slow decisions and tie up billable time.

Industry observers note that siteAI Drafter allows people to draw their own road network and configure lots while the system enforces basic subdivision rules in the background. The tool understands roads and rights of way, lot dimensions and product mix so users can experiment with different layouts while staying within buildable constraints.

According to Prophetic, SiteAI Drafter enables land teams to:.

The result is a customizable subdivision plan that can reflect the specific community a builder wants to take to a seller, investment committee or municipal review, while still providing a defensible yield number.

Beyond drafting, Prophetic is adding CAD export so that prepares created either by SiteAI’s automated engine or by SiteAI Drafter can be used as a starting point for detailed civil engineering design.

Sources indicate that this is intended to shift engineers and planners away from redrawing concepts from scratch and toward refining the land team’s preferred layout. Prophetic remarked the export capability also opens the platform to civil engineers, planners and land developers who want to generate quick concepts before full design or to show builders what a site can hold before a first meeting.

“Every land team looks a site a little differently,” said Oliver Alexander, founder and CEO of Prophetic. “Sometimes you want an answer in seconds across dozens of parcels. Sometimes you already know exactly where the entry and the main road go, and you want to see what your blueprint yields. SiteAI now works however you do. And with CAD export, the plan doesn’t stop with the land team. It goes to the engineer as a starting point, not a sketch to redraw. That’s what an operating system for land acquisition should do: carry the work forward and help our users win more deals.”.

Industry observers note that as higher rates and tighter capital make land bets more costly, builders, developers and their capital partners are under pressure to vet more sites with fewer people and less time. Early engineering work is expensive, and using consultants for preliminary concepts can slow down offers in competitive bid situations.

Tools that combine automated yield analysis with guided drafting give acquisition leaders a way to pressure-test their preferred community design before committing to full engineering fees. For homebuilders and land developers, the ability to walk into a seller or investment committee meeting with a concept proposal, yield range and CAD-ready file can help shorten decision cycles and reduce the risk of surprises later in entitlement or design.

Base Switches Off Flashblocks as Denim Goes Live: The Migration Risks Behind 200ms Blocks

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1253 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that base's Denim upgrade replaced Flashblocks with five canonical blocks per second.
  • For about sixteen months, Base's fastest blocks were only promises.
  • Denim went live on Base mainnet on November 5, after activating on Sepolia on October 21.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

It has been revealed that base's Denim upgrade replaced Flashblocks with five canonical blocks per second. What that means for sequencers, RPC providers and smart contract developers is where the real story sits.

For about sixteen months, Base's fastest blocks were only promises. Since November 5, they are the ledger itself.

Denim went live on Base mainnet on November 5, after activating on Sepolia on October 21.

According to the upgrade page, the chain now produces five complete canonical blocks every second instead of one every two seconds. Flashblocks, the preconfirmation layer that ran alongside the two-second blocks since July 2025, is retired.

Most coverage stopped at the speed figure. The sharper question is what separates a canonical block from a preconfirmation, because that gap decides what breaks and what improves for anyone building on the chain.

It has been revealed that those updates were the sequencer's early word on what the next block would contain. They were previews of pending state, and nothing in them had its own hash, state root or receipts until the two-second block was sealed. Developers therefore had to keep an early execution result mentally separate from a settled transaction.

Denim turns the 200ms unit into the real thing. Under Base's 200ms Native Blocks specification, every block carries its own number, hash, state root, receipts and forkchoice updates, and moves through the unsafe, safe and finalized stages like any other block.

Sources indicate that the sequencer's job gets heavier and stricter. Instead of streaming fragments of a larger block, it has to build and execute a full block for every 200ms slot. The header keeps its timestamp in whole seconds, so Denim adds a metadata transaction, the BaseTime deposit, placed second in every block. It supplies the sub-second portion: 0, 200, 400, 600 or 800 milliseconds.

It has been revealed that timing rules are tight. Slots can't be skipped, and each block's full timestamp must land exactly 200ms after its parent's. That timestamp comes from a schedule tied to the Denim activation and the block number, not from the sequencer's clock, so wall-clock time only determines when a build begins. Once execution finishes, the client rejects any block that breaks the 200ms progression.

It has been revealed that this removes a layer of ambiguity. A preconfirmation was only as strong as the sequencer's word, while a canonical block can be validated, replayed and challenged by any node running the same derivation rules.

It has been revealed that app developers face the biggest practical shift. Flashblocks streams ended at activation, so anything built on newFlashblocks, pendingLogs or the pending block tag has to move to canonical subscriptions like newHeads and logs. The migration guide lists the API changes required.

Industry observers note that the seconds-based timestamp field stays as it was for compatibility. Block, header, transaction, log and receipt responses now include optional millisecond fields, timestampMs and blockTimestampMs, derived from authenticated BaseTime data. They are left out when that data has been pruned or is unavailable. One tooling detail deserves attention: the spec warns that the plain Alloy AnyRpcHeader type drops unknown fields, so anyone who needs millisecond timestamps must use a different type.

Recent findings suggest that node providers will see heavier traffic too. Dwellir's analysis notes that any service doing work on every block now does it ten times as often. Five fetches a second replace one every two seconds. Denim improves latency without adding capacity, so infrastructure bills are likely to climb.

Sources indicate that finality hasn't gone away either. Faster production doesn't erase the confirmation policy an application picks, and each 200ms block still passes through the same unsafe, safe and finalized stages. Bridges and exchanges that wait for a specific stage before crediting funds may need to rethink how many blocks they wait for, since a block count no longer equals the same stretch of time.

This is the area that deserves the most urgent attention. Base's spec warns that block.number now advances ten times faster in real time, while block.timestamp still ticks in whole seconds. A contract that treats a block count as a duration will see that duration collapse to a tenth of what its authors intended.

According to recent reports, the affected patterns are common ones. Timelocks and cooldowns measured in blocks expire in a tenth of the time. Vesting and emission schedules run ten times faster. Per-block rate limits reset five times a second instead of once every two seconds, which lifts the effective per-second limit tenfold. Governance voting windows set in blocks shrink the same way. Uniswap V3-style TWAP oracles stay accurate, but a fixed observation cardinality now covers less wall-clock history, so long lookbacks can revert sooner.

Recent findings suggest that contracts built on block.timestamp are unaffected. Where a block count can be adjusted through governance, teams blueprint to divide it by ten. Where it is hardcoded into an immutable contract, the spec indicates it can't be retuned after activation, which leaves migration as the only fix. Denim also tightens transfer rules for Base's B20 token standard, and transfers to a token's own address now revert.

In a recent development, the coming weeks will show how much of this stays theoretical. Three things are worth tracking: whether any immutable contract with block-count logic misbehaves, how providers cope with the jump in per-block requests, and whether apps built around Flashblocks have fully moved over.

Denim looks like a cleaner design than the layer it replaced. A preview mechanism gives way to a block anyone can verify, and developers pay for it with a real migration. Speed grabbed the headlines, but the lasting change is that Base's sub-second confirmations now stand on the same footing as the chain's ordinary blocks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 13, 2026 at 7:24 amNovember 13, 2026 at 4:23 pm.
  • It has been revealed that updated at 4 p.m.
  • If emails sent by Outlook consumers on Thursday are just now landing in your inbox, no, you haven’t gone back to the days of the Pony Express.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 13, 2026 at 7:24 amNovember 13, 2026 at 4:23 pm.

It has been revealed that updated at 4 p.m. PT Nov. 13 with additional Microsoft statements.

If emails sent by Outlook consumers on Thursday are just now landing in your inbox, no, you haven’t gone back to the days of the Pony Express. Microsoft is still digging out from a nearly daylong outage that cut off email for businesses, schools and governments around the world.

As of early Friday, the company reported that email queues were “significantly reduced and approaching normal levels,” though some owners could still have trouble getting in or see delayed messages.

In a post on X Friday morning, Microsoft remarked it was “deeply sorry” for the disruption to customers and partners. The manufacturer said the outage was a technical issue, not related to a cyberattack or AI agents.

The problem was introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and surfaced after a more recent network change, the organization said, adding that it has addressed the underlying issue and is still restoring service to remaining customers and regions.

Sources indicate that we are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.This was a technical matter….

In an update on its status page at 5 a.m. Pacific, Microsoft remarked it was seeing “broader improvements now observed in North America and sustained improvements across much of Europe,” along with early signs of recovery in Asia Pacific.

The problems started Thursday morning with Exchange Online, the Microsoft service that runs Outlook email for businesses, and spread to other Microsoft 365 services that depend on it, including Teams calendars, Copilot and SharePoint.

According to recent reports, microsoft said servers were failing automated health checks and dropping out of service, which overloaded the ones that were left. The tech giant paused all deployments while it worked on a fix, and some of its repairs Thursday evening were “not taking as expected.” Microsoft said it restored service gradually, checking stability at each stage, which took longer but helped ensure a stable restoration.

Earlier, The Verge’s Tom Warren reported on X that his sources linked the outage to configuration changes in Azure Virtual Network, Microsoft’s cloud networking service.

Australia’s Home Affairs Minister, Tony Burke, told reporters in Sydney that Microsoft believes it is dealing with something similar in some ways to the 2024 CrowdStrike outage, “where there is an update that has gone awry,” the Associated Press reported.

According to recent reports, “We know our customers rely on our services to get important work done every day, and regret the impact these outages had on those who depend on us,” said Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, in a statement provided to GeekWire. He said Microsoft’s teams are reviewing what happened and how to prevent similar problems.

In a post on X Friday afternoon, Lamanna mentioned the investigation points to “cascading failures + thundering herds at our network perimeter,” which made recovery harder than normal. A thundering herd happens when large numbers of clients try to reconnect at the same time, overwhelming systems as they come back online.

He remarked Microsoft will publish a post-mortem “shortly” with a step-by-step timeline and the repairs it plans to make to avoid similar outages.

According to recent reports, the outage reached well beyond email. Government offices in Japan, Singapore and the Philippines reported disruptions, according to the AP. Workhorse Group delayed its quarterly earnings call, and OpenAI and Anthropic both reported problems connecting with Microsoft 365 tools.

In a recent development, credit rating agency Morningstar DBRS estimated insured losses of $300 million to $500 million, well below estimates for CrowdStrike, which ranged from $400 million to $1.5 billion. Some cyber insurance policies cover only malicious attacks, the firm noted, though it said the toll could grow if the outage drags on for several days.

Recent findings suggest that the disruption hit close to Microsoft’s home. Ansel Herz, a spokesperson for the Seattle mayor’s office, told the Seattle Times that the outage didn’t bring city government to a halt but knocked out the systems that move documents and messages around City Hall.

The newspaper quoted Herz calling the outage “a huge pain.” In a post on X, he chided the paper for not using his whole quote, which we presume was “a huge pain in the ass.”.

In a recent development, we’ve followed up with him to confirm this notable detail. Here’s hoping he gets the email.

Patch, 10 a.m.: Herz did receive GeekWire’s message and responded, confirming the quote and saying that, to his knowledge, nothing public-facing was affected at the city. Email appears to be back and working properly as of Friday morning, he said.

Latest Update: How reverse mortgage LOs can help borrowers to self-service

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Reverse mortgage servicers are investing in portals, mobile applications and smarter phone systems so borrowers can manage their loans without contacting a human customer service representative.
  • Gail Balettie, senior vice president of client satisfaction at Celink, and Ryan McIntire, director of reverse mortgage servicing controls at Onity Mortgage, outlined their companies’ self-service offerings during a panel discussion moderated by Chris Downey of CrossCountry Mortgage at last week’s National Reverse Mortgage Lenders Association (NRMLA) Annual Meeting & Expo.
  • “In today’s world, where we are conditioned to some extent to be able to go online, get immediate satisfaction, to do things without talking to somebody, the more we can do that, the better we can reach our customers,” McIntire said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reverse mortgage servicers are investing in portals, mobile applications and smarter phone systems so borrowers can manage their loans without contacting a human customer service representative. Servicing executives say that loan officers can play a key role in whether these tools actually work.

Gail Balettie, senior vice president of client satisfaction at Celink, and Ryan McIntire, director of reverse mortgage servicing controls at Onity Mortgage, outlined their companies’ self-service offerings during a panel discussion moderated by Chris Downey of CrossCountry Mortgage at last week’s National Reverse Mortgage Lenders Association (NRMLA) Annual Meeting & Expo.

“In today’s world, where we are conditioned to some extent to be able to go online, get immediate satisfaction, to do things without talking to somebody, the more we can do that, the better we can reach our customers,” McIntire said.

In a recent development, balettie announced at NRMLA Annual that her manufacturer’s mobile app, ReverseLink, will be launching “in the next few weeks.” Its design is similar to Celink’s website and borrowers will receive an invitation to download it. The company is the largest independent subservicer of reverse mortgages and has an estimated market share of about 75% across federally insured Home Equity Conversion Mortgages (HECMs) and proprietary loans.

Industry observers note that mcIntire told the audience that Onity‘s servicing app is already available on iPhone and Android devices and mirrors its borrower portal. He stressed the importance of providing familiar technology to senior homeowners so “they don’t feel like they’re having to learn something all over again.”.

Sources indicate that celink’s soon-to-be-released app will allow clients to accomplish multiple tasks, Balettie noted. They’ll be able to request payoff quotes, make voluntary payments, upload forms and download up to two years of statements. The app automatically generates confirmation that an uploaded form has been received, cutting down the number of calls needed for this purpose.

“They can request a line-of-credit draw, and if they do so, they’re going to get their funds a day or two faster than the typical five-day turn time, because it comes in an automated fashion,” she added.

ReverseLink also has a number of FAQs and educational videos, covering subjects like how to manage the account online, what happens to the reverse mortgage when the borrower dies, how to shop for insurance coverage and how to file a claim, and how to find help with small home repairs.

Onity’s portal ties into the tech giant’s system of record, McIntire stated. It demonstrates three months of transactions and includes an introduction package that’s tailored to the structure of the loan — for example, any funds set aside for required repairs. Onity is also in the process of building fully digital draw request forms. Today, borrowers have to download and complete these forms before returning it via email or fax, but the goal is to process e-signed draw requests within a few business days, McIntire said.

It has been revealed that “Obviously, information that’s available to the borrower via this site is very sensitive. We obviously, as servicers, have to be very cognizant and mindful of fraud. So it does have multifactor authentication that just helps provide that additional sense of security,” he added.

Borrowers commonly contact their loan officer, rather than their servicer, when they have questions about their loan. Balettie said that LOs can take an “ABCD” role to approach to providing assistance in this area.

Making sure a servicer has the correct contact information for a borrower may seem obvious, but it doesn’t happen with perfect uniformity. “We get about 70% of our loans that board with an email address. I want to see that be 100%,” Balettie noted. “I don’t know very many people who don’t have an email address in this day and age.”.

According to recent reports, balettie sought to distinguish between the alternate contact on the loan application and an authorized third party. The latter may discuss the account but cannot change contact information or request a draw or payoff. Conversely, servicers use the alternate contact only when they cannot reach the borrower, she said.

Sources indicate that in response to an audience question, Balettie said that loan officers are welcome to call a servicer on their client’s behalf, but to receive a relevant response, they must be listed as the authorized third party. This is especially notable for brokers, who lose access to information once a loan is sold. “We have privacy laws we have to follow,” she added.

According to recent reports, A power of attorney can act for a living borrower, but legal authority ends at death, the panelists noted. Downey urged originators to execute the authorized party form at closing and warned that without it, payoffs for a borrower “can be a nightmare.” Having this information on file removes the need to hire an attorney to search for heirs after the borrower dies.

Balettie noted originators should collect a canceled check and the direct deposit form at closing. Borrowers without a check can provide a redacted bank statement or bank letter with their account and routing numbers. Due to security concerns, servicers don’t allow bank details to be added online, but they’ll accept faxed or emailed documents, and closing is the best time to gather them.

Dark Matter, ServiceLink add automated closing to Empower

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dark Matter Technologies and ServiceLink have partnered to bring automated title, valuation and closing services to lenders using Dark Matter’s Empower loan origination system.
  • Recent findings suggest that the partnership integrates ServiceLink’s Accelerated Close platform, powered by its NowIntelligence technology, into Empower.
  • According to recent reports, using loan data, Accelerated Close automatically determines whether a loan qualifies for an expedited workflow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dark Matter Technologies and ServiceLink have partnered to bring automated title, valuation and closing services to lenders using Dark Matter’s Empower loan origination system.

Recent findings suggest that the partnership integrates ServiceLink’s Accelerated Close platform, powered by its NowIntelligence technology, into Empower. The service automates title and valuation orders, as well as closing orders, and allows lenders or borrowers to schedule appraisals and closings.

According to recent reports, using loan data, Accelerated Close automatically determines whether a loan qualifies for an expedited workflow. NowIntelligence evaluates eligibility using real-time market intelligence, including public and proprietary data, vendor information and market analytics.

Industry observers note that for eligible loans, Empower automatically places title and valuation orders with ServiceLink through Exchange, Dark Matter’s partner marketplace. Once a loan reaches clear-to-close status, closing orders are also placed automatically through Empower.

The companies said the integration reduces manual work for lender operations teams and can shorten the time between underwriting approval and a scheduled closing.

Borrower expectations are also driving demand for faster and more flexible closing processes. According to ServiceLink’s 2026 State of Homebuying Report, 82% of borrowers believe a refinance should take less than a month to close, while 87% said the ability to schedule their own appraisal or closing would influence their choice of lender.

It has been revealed that “Borrowers judge their lender by how fast and frictionless the process feels, and knowing when their appraisal and closing will happen matters a great deal,” stated Vikas Rao, CEO of Dark Matter Technologies. “Accelerated Close takes routine ordering off lenders’ plates and, if desired, puts scheduling in borrowers’ hands, so loans close faster and borrowers feel in control of one of the biggest financial decisions of their lives.”.

ServiceLink CEO Chris Azur stated the integration is intended to help lenders shorten cycle times, improve pull-through rates and provide borrowers with a more streamlined experience.

It has been revealed that for lenders, shorter cycle times could also reduce costs associated with extended rate locks. Orders placed through ServiceLink will continue to use the existing Exchange workflow for order status updates, documents and messaging.

Lenders can enable Accelerated Close through their Dark Matter or ServiceLink account managers, through self-service configuration or as part of a newly introduced Empower implementation, the companies’ release stated.

Uncommon Thinkers: Alexis Harroun aims for space with a new engine — and stays grounded

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1399 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 13, 2026 at 7:46 amNovember 17, 2026 at 7:48 am.
  • Editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec.
  • Industry observers note that A few weeks after learning that her tiny startup had won a NASA prize to fly its engine in space, Alexis Harroun was camping in Yellowstone, sitting around a fire and looking up at the stars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 13, 2026 at 7:46 amNovember 17, 2026 at 7:48 am.

Editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec. 10 at the GeekWire Gala in partnership with Greater Seattle Partners.

Industry observers note that A few weeks after learning that her tiny startup had won a NASA prize to fly its engine in space, Alexis Harroun was camping in Yellowstone, sitting around a fire and looking up at the stars. Satellites kept drifting past overhead — and the news finally sank in.

“I’m like, oh, we’re going to be sending something up and we’re going to be able to see it,” she mentioned. “That was very humbling in a lot of ways and very exciting.”.

Industry observers note that harroun is co-founder and CEO of Juno Propulsion, a Tukwila, Wash.-based startup building a new kind of rocket engine. Instead of a steady flame, Juno’s engines use detonation, a supersonic combustion wave that releases more energy from the same amount of propellant.

“It’s essentially like a higher MPG rocket engine,” Harroun said.

The technology has been studied for decades but has never flown in orbit. Juno aims to change that next year, when its engine is set to fly aboard a Momentus satellite in a mission called Project Iris.

That’s a massive goal for a company that, when the July 2025 NASA call came, was just Harroun, co-founder and CTO Ari Martinez and a summer intern working out of a one-room office.

If Iris succeeds, Juno’s engines could let satellites run on non-toxic propellants and maneuver far more freely in orbit, something both commercial and defense customers increasingly want. For Harroun, who earned her Ph.D. studying these engines, it would be the payoff of years of work.

Harroun sees the technology as a long-overdue leap. The basic physics behind today’s rocket engines dates to the 1930s and has been refined about as far as it can go, she remarked, calling it a constraint that’s “been a glass ceiling for too long, in my opinion.”.

According to recent reports, harroun grew up south of Seattle in Federal Way. She didn’t come from an aerospace family or spend her childhood dreaming about space. Her dad was a physician and her mom a flight attendant and flight instructor.

Industry observers note that what she did pick up at home was an entrepreneurial streak. Her dad ran his own practice for about 20 years, and her mom is now a real estate agent. Harroun stated watching them make “something out of completely nothing” has shaped her own path, especially in building Juno.

It has been revealed that she calls herself a “late bloomer” who fell for engineering as she was finishing high school and heading to the University of Washington. Sci-fi became an inspiration along the way, and it’s now one of her favorite genres.

She spent all four years at UW working with professor Carl Knowlen, who leads the Aeronautics & Astronautics Department’s Detonation Engines Lab, and she joined the student rocketry team, eventually leading its propulsion group.

Knowlen “sees the potential in everyone,” Harroun said, and the two built a strong relationship that’s still going. Juno’s $1.2 million National Science Foundation grant, awarded this summer, is a partnership with his research group.

Knowlen was also the faculty adviser for the student rocketry team, where he spent “many hot, and sometimes rainy, days” with Harroun and her teammates, test-firing motors and launching high-powered rockets.

According to recent reports, “She always was level-headed and led by example,” Knowlen stated. “No one worked harder than her to see these tests and introduces go off as planned.”.

He called her “an exceptional student, natural leader, creative thinker, and very independent,” and mentioned it’s been a great satisfaction to see the engineer she has become.

During college, Harroun interned at NASA, Boeing and Blue Origin. That first stint at Blue Origin, in 2016, set her next move.

“I realized that everyone who had the job that I wanted had gone to Purdue,” she noted.

In a recent development, she spent the next six years at Purdue University in West Lafayette, Ind., earning a master’s degree and a Ph.D. Her doctoral research was on the technology Juno is now building. She also met Martinez there. The two shared an office for years.

Harroun never planned to stay in academia.

“That just didn’t feel like my calling,” she said. “I wanted to use that very unique experience to get the technical chops to do the type of engineering that I wanted to do.”.

Her doctoral advisor, Purdue professor Stephen Heister, still advises her and the manufacturer.

“He was one of the people who really pushed me to think about starting this tech giant,” Harroun remarked. “I think he saw the potential that I had as a founder, both from a technical and a leadership perspective.”.

Industry observers note that heister recalled their first technical discussion, when Harroun arrived as a latest master’s student. He went deep on nozzle flows, her thesis topic, and the complications of building a nozzle for a detonation engine.

“At the end of my diatribe, she sat quietly and noted, ‘You’ve given me a lot to think about,’” Heister said. “I can’t think of any other 22-year-old student with such a response but I knew she was indeed a special talent.”.

He described Harroun as having “the unique ability to think deeply and at length,” and stated it’s “terribly gratifying” to watch her commercialize the technology she worked on as a grad student.

Industry observers note that after finishing her Ph.D. in 2023, Harroun came back to the Seattle region and started Juno. She knew the territory: her UW lab work and the rocketry team had put her in touch with local industry, and Juno now works with some of the same companies she did as a student.

Interning at Blue Origin was the first time she could say “there’s literally a rocket organization in our backyard,” Harroun mentioned. Its presence helped build a regional talent pool, which she described as “a contingent of rocket scientists that just live here.”.

Starting a tech giant comes with many unknowns, and coming home crossed one off the list.

In a recent development, “I knew how to go start doing stuff immediately,” she noted. “So it made that calculus really easy.”.

Harroun’s ambitions reach well beyond one demo flight.

“Our mission is to be the rocket engine provider for the U.S.,” she mentioned. “Think of a Rocketdyne.”.

That firm built engines for the Saturn V and the space shuttle, and it’s now part of L3Harris. Juno wants to play a similar role with a new technology. It’s starting with in-space propulsion for satellites and intends to expand into engines for upper stages, orbital transfer vehicles and, eventually, the boosters that lift rockets off the pad.

The first step is Project Iris. NASA paid Juno about $500,000 through its TechLeap program to build the payload, and it’s also covering the Momentus spacecraft and the flight. There’s no paying customer yet, but the mission is designed to mimic the maneuvers a real satellite would make.

Industry observers note that japan’s space agency has flown rotating detonation engines on suborbital research rockets, but going to orbit is “a whole ‘nother game,” Harroun noted. “Going to space is hard. I can attest to that.”.

Building a firm has taught Harroun things her Ph.D. didn’t. Handling toxic propellants is so complicated, she learned, that operators can spend more fueling a satellite than on “the propulsion system itself, which is kind of crazy.”.

The bigger draw is mobility. For decades, satellites have mostly stayed in the orbit a rocket left them in, she remarked, and “that’s not really acceptable anymore in today’s world.”.

To get there, Juno has raised a $1.4 million pre-seed round led by SOSV, on top of its NASA and NSF awards.

As for going to space herself, Harroun admits it would be hard to say no if she got the opportunity.

Industry observers note that but the avid hiker and backpacker is partial to terra firma. Her best-case future is one where Earth is the place humanity gets to enjoy and space is what makes that possible.

“I don’t know that I would be the traveler,” Harroun mentioned, “but I’d definitely like to be the enabler.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

XRP has continued to fall to levels not seen in the last three months as prolonged market volatility continues to intensify, causing the asset to post bigger daily price losses.

While momentum appears to be fading rapidly, the slow price movements have caused expectations for a November recovery to weaken, especially among prediction market traders.

Latest data from leading prediction market Kalshi highlights that XRP traders have little confidence that the asset can still reclaim $1.30 before the end of the month.

While the asset saw higher expectations from Kalshi traders last month, it appears that its recent price dip below $1 has lowered their expectations as traders are assigning low probabilities to XRP reaching higher price targets this month.

Following their predictions, XRP presently has 7% odds of trading above $1.40, while the probability of reaching $1.50 stands at 8%.

More notably, bets on XRP surging to around $1.60 are even weaker, with only a 4% implied probability, suggesting that traders have increasingly lost confidence in XRP’s potential to achieve a major recovery before this month runs out.

The weak XRP predictions from Kalshi traders have come as XRP struggles to maintain momentum around its recent price levels, falling substantially below its local highs.

As of the time of writing, XRP is trading around $0.9892, representing a substantial decline of about 3.94% over the past 24 hours and an 11.3% drop over the last week.

It is important to note that the Kalshi data only reflects traders' positioning amid current market conditions and therefore does not guarantee XRP’s precise price movement in the future.

While XRP has continued to struggle below the major $1 level, it would need to stage a major recovery to reclaim the $1.30 level.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andrew Yakubik, D.C., examines how structural limitations and functional limitations affect movement and contribute to ongoing discomfort.

In a recent development, WACO, Texas, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What causes neck and shoulder pain, and how do structural limitations and functional limitations influence treatment? That question is answered in a HelloNation article featuring insights from Andrew Yakubik, D.C., of Anthony Medical & Chiropractic Center in Waco, Texas.

The HelloNation article explains that neck and shoulder pain often develop together because these areas share muscles, joints, and movement patterns. When one area is affected, it can swiftly influence the other, making it notable to understand the underlying causes before beginning neck and shoulder pain treatment.

The article describes structural limitations as physical restrictions within the joints or spine that limit normal movement. These may include joint stiffness, misalignment, or degenerative changes that reduce the range of motion. Individuals experiencing structural limitations may notice persistent stiffness or difficulty turning the head or lifting the arm without discomfort.

Functional limitations are different and relate to how muscles and surrounding tissues work together during movement. The article notes that even when the joint structure is intact, poor coordination or muscle imbalance can lead to inefficient movement patterns. Over time, this can place added stress on certain areas and contribute to ongoing neck and shoulder pain.

The HelloNation article emphasizes that effective neck and shoulder pain treatment often requires addressing both structural limitations and functional limitations. Focusing on only one aspect may leave underlying issues unresolved, increasing the likelihood of recurring discomfort.

Posture is highlighted as a key factor in the development of both types of limitations. The article explains that forward head posture and rounded shoulders can place continuous strain on the neck and upper back. This strain can lead to joint restriction and muscle imbalance, reinforcing patterns that contribute to chronic neck and shoulder pain.

Muscle imbalance is another notable factor discussed in the article. When some muscles become overactive while others weaken, movement becomes less efficient and more stressful on the joints. This imbalance can reduce range of motion and increase discomfort during daily activities, making posture correction and targeted care essential parts of treatment.

It has been revealed that the article notes that a proper clinical evaluation is necessary to determine whether structural limitations, functional limitations, or both are contributing to the condition. This evaluation may include assessing the range of motion, observing movement patterns, and identifying areas of weakness or restriction.

Treatment approaches often combine multiple strategies to address both structure and function. The HelloNation article explains that joint-focused care may help improve mobility and reduce stiffness, while corrective exercises can help retrain muscles and restore more balanced movement patterns. This coordinated approach supports more consistent progress.

Consistency is also emphasized as an important part of neck and shoulder pain treatment. The article explains that improving movement patterns and joint function takes time, especially when habits have developed over long periods. A structured blueprint that addresses both structural limitations and functional limitations can help support steady and lasting improvement.

It has been revealed that the article concludes that understanding the difference between structural and functional issues provides valuable insight into why neck and shoulder pain develop. By focusing on both aspects, care becomes more precise and better aligned with the root causes of discomfort, leading to improved mobility and long-term outcomes.

Recent findings suggest that the Clinical Approach to Neck and Shoulder Pain: Identifying Structural vs. Functional Limitations features insights from Andrew Yakubik, D.C., Chiropractic Care Expert of Waco, Texas, in HelloNation.

Homebuilder confidence sinks to a 14-year low as buyers hibernate

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Homebuilder confidence fell in November to its lowest point since the latter days of the Global Financial Crisis, as elevated mortgage rates, persistent inflation and buyer hesitancy continue to weigh on demand.
  • The National Association of Home Builders (NAHB)/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (HMI) fell four points to 25 in November, representing the weakest homebuilder confidence reading since April 2012.
  • It has been revealed that builders have relied ever more heavily on discounts and mortgage buydown tactics to move inventory, with NAHB reporting that 46% of builders cut prices during the month, the highest share since the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Homebuilder confidence fell in November to its lowest point since the latter days of the Global Financial Crisis, as elevated mortgage rates, persistent inflation and buyer hesitancy continue to weigh on demand.

The National Association of Home Builders (NAHB)/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (HMI) fell four points to 25 in November, representing the weakest homebuilder confidence reading since April 2012.

It has been revealed that builders have relied ever more heavily on discounts and mortgage buydown tactics to move inventory, with NAHB reporting that 46% of builders cut prices during the month, the highest share since the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic. Typical discounts ran flat at 6% for the eighth straight month, and 68% of builders used sales incentives, another post-Covid high. It was the 20th consecutive month that at least 60% of builders had featured margin-eroding price-cut promotions.

Further, in November, all three of the key HMI components sank. The index of current sales conditions declined six points to 28, while the measure of sales expectations over the next six months slipped two points to 30, signaling a prolonged pessimistic outlook. Meanwhile, the gauge of prospective buyer traffic dropped two points to 16, the lowest level in 15 years outside of the early months of the pandemic in 2020.

It has been revealed that “Builders are confronting multiple challenges in today’s economy,” NAHB Chairman Bill Owens, a home builder and remodeler from Worthington, Ohio, noted in a statement. “Stepped-up immigration enforcement is keeping legal workers off job sites, deepening labor shortages and driving up costs. Higher fuel prices are prompting subcontractors to raise their rates sharply, and with fewer buyers in the market, more builders are scaling back construction.”.

NAHB Chief Economist Robert Dietz stated in a statement that a combination of policy and macroeconomic pressures is straining both supply and demand.

“The housing market faces a range of supply-side challenges, including building material costs pushed higher by tariffs, an ongoing shortage of construction workers and excessive regulations that undermine housing affordability,” Dietz stated. “Mortgage rates above 7%, softer consumer confidence and an uncertain economic outlook are holding buyers back.”.

Public homebuilders echoed that picture on recent earnings calls, citing hesitant buyers, heavier discounting and thinner margins.

Century Communities Executive Chairman Dale Francescon, during an earnings call on October 28, noted that high mortgage rates, continued inflation and macroeconomic uncertainty weighed heavily on consumer confidence, particularly among first-time buyers.

“As we moved through the quarter, our buyers became more cautious, did not feel an urgency to transact and felt more comfortable moving to the sidelines,” Francescon mentioned during the call.

It’s not that buyers have abandoned the market. Rather, they are waiting out volatility and elongating decision-making timelines. At the same time, the number of households that can qualify for a mortgage at today’s borrowing costs and sales prices continues to shrink.

LGI Homes chairman and CEO Eric Lipar noted the increasingly challenging market conditions during an earnings call on November 3.

According to recent reports, “As expected, the market became more challenging as the quarter progressed,” Lipar said. “Affordability remained the defining story of the quarter.”.

The homebuilder, which primarily serves rate- and payment-sensitive entry-level buyers, reported a cancellation rate of 53.8%, compared with 33.6% a year earlier and 26.2% two years ago. While this trend was an outlier among most of its public homebuilding peers, it underscores how strained entry-level buyers are right now.

During PulteGroup’s earnings call on October 22, the builder’s president and CEO Ryan Marshall agreed that market conditions have become more challenging in recent months, leading many buyers to put their homebuying process on the back burner.

“What changed in the quarter…is that the major move higher in interest rates, along with inflation, global tensions, and waning confidence, reached the point where more consumers simply put their search on pause,” he stated during the call.

Traffic to PulteGroup communities fell 14% year over year and 11% sequentially in the third quarter, with first-time buyers making up most of the missing traffic.

Marshall also noted that, with 30-year mortgage rates still sitting at around 7.5%, move-up buyers are increasingly having a difficult time selling their current home, further dragging on homebuying demand.

“One of the biggest impediments that we’re seeing right now is that our move-up and active-adult buyers need to sell their existing home, and that is tough,” Marshall noted.

In a recent development, with homeownership increasingly out of reach for the average working American, renting has become the more affordable option. Zillow research found that renting a home costs more than $1,000 less per month than buying one, a gap that draws many would-be buyers away from for-sale homebuilders and toward the rental market.

For many homebuilders, winning over cautious buyers now means resorting to more and more incentives, in effect paying for sales. Concessions are climbing, and total sales prices are coming down with them. The median new-home sales price in September was about $400,000, down nearly 4.0% from a year ago.

Builders continue to use mortgage rate buydowns as a sales tool, and the numbers show it. A recent Realtor.com report found that the average fresh-home buyer had a starting mortgage rate of 5.01% during the third quarter, compared with 6.15% for existing-home buyers.

Recent findings suggest that century Communities is among the builders leaning hard on incentives to facilitate sales. The company reported that, during Q3, incentives averaged about 13.0% of the total sales price, up from 12% in Q2 and 11.0%. The builder’s CFO Scott Dixon noted on an October earnings call that incentives will likely rise in the fourth quarter as Century pushes to meet its year-end goals.

“We expect incentives on closed homes in the fourth quarter of 2026 to be 200-250 basis points higher than third quarter levels as we navigate a higher rate environment, muted consumer confidence and compete with other builders for year-end closings,” he stated during the call.

Meritage Homes Executive Vice President and CFO Hilla Sferruzza concurred that the incentive environment is likely to stay elevated for some time, as she addressed analysts on an October 29 earnings call. The builder continues to use incentives and price discounts, with its average closing price down 4% year over year to $365,000.

“Absent a sustained market-driven catalyst that provides meaningful mortgage rate relief, we expect incentives to remain at this elevated level for the near term,” Sferruzza noted.

On the other hand, during a session at the HousingWire Homebuilder Summit last month, Taylor Morrison CEO Sheryl Palmer warned that homebuilders have trained today’s buyers to expect more and more concessions.

In a recent development, “We, as builders, created this environment,” Palmer said during the session. “We created this place where the longer the house has been sitting there, the more we’re going to give you.”.

In a recent development, for builders, the question is how much profit they are willing to trade for sales. Those who protect margins risk losing volume, while those who chase volume are watching margins thin.

Most public homebuilders reported lower gross profit margins in the third quarter than a year earlier, including:.

Beyond the immediate sales and margin challenges, many homebuilders are struggling to determine how much inventory to carry and what their 2027 production plans should look like.

Meritage Homes, for example, declined to give formal Q3 guidance, arguing that volatile market conditions limit their visibility.

PulteGroup’s President and CEO Ryan Marshall agreed that “the current environment has made it a more difficult planning time.”.

According to recent reports, and D.R. Horton Executive Vice President Jessica Hansen echoed this sentiment during an October 29 earnings call.

“Given the uncertainty in these conditions and the broader economy, our initial fiscal 2027 guidance reflects wider ranges than usual,” Hansen explained.

Builders have navigated this challenging market by cutting cycle times, extracting costs, improving floor prepares and leveraging AI to improve operational efficiency. What’s out of their control is whether buyers feel ready to commit, or when that will change.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 13, 2026 at 12:51 pmNovember 13, 2026 at 4:38 pm.

Araceli Biosciences, a Portland-area biotech company, has secured $4.5 million in funding to help commercialize technology and develop fresh products that support using human cells instead of animal studies to test new drugs.

According to recent reports, the Tigard, Ore., startup offers instruments and software for creating images of cells and automating analysis. Its technologies fall under the umbrella term “Fresh Approach Methodologies,” which includes human-tissue models, computer simulations and AI-based approaches that reduce or avoid experimentation on animals such as mice, rats and monkeys.

Supporters of the methods, known as NAMs, argue that they can yield better outcomes because animals are not a perfect substitute for humans and can generate irrelevant findings. That can lead to costly, time-intensive development of drugs that fail to perform in people. Advocates also promote the alternatives as more humane.

The National Institutes of Health revealed $84 million in September to build infrastructure for NAMs research at 10 sites nationwide.

“[T]he efforts signal a significant investment into human-based technologies as the future of preclinical science, aiming to make research faster, more predictive, and more directly relevant to human health,” the NIH stated in a release.

Araceli mentioned it has raised a total of $22.7 million from investors. The fresh round was led by William Cortelyou and included Fluke Venture Partners, according to PitchBook. The company disclosed Thursday that businessman and animal welfare advocate Jeff Swickard was also an investor.

Swickard owns 54 auto dealerships across Western states and is a commercial real estate investor with $250 million invested in Portland properties.

Shawn MacDonald, chief financial officer for Araceli, noted Swickard’s “support reflects a belief that we share, which is that better science and more humane science go hand-in-hand.”.

Araceli launched in 2023 as a spinoff from Phoseon Technology, which makes UV LED units for industrial curing and life sciences applications.

The manufacturer remarked that companies and institutions using Araceli technology include the Max Planck Institute and Evotec in Germany, the Wertheim UF Scripps Institute in Florida, VALID Therapeutics in Boston, and Ginkgo Bioworks, as well as large pharmaceutical companies. It has 30 employees.
